newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Dec 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Dec 20.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Retired Cape Town advocate Bertrand Hoberman SC was removed by the Cape Supreme Court on Thursday as commissioner of the section 417 inquiry into the collapsed Tollgate group after it was found he acted with bias against banking group Absa (Amalgamated Banks of South Africa).
- Inflation rose slightly to 9.2 percent last month from October's 9.1 percent, raising hopes that double digits might be avoided in the present upward cycle.

- South African officials would hand over a document to the European Union on Friday outlining Pretoria's position on the impending EU-South Africa talks on a co-operation agreement, including a free trade area, South African embassy counselor John Mare said on Thursday.

- Production in the beleaguered footwear industry fell to the levels of the 1970s this year, with 35 million pairs of shoes produced, down 16 percent from last year, Dennis Linde, director of the Footwear Manufactureres Federation of South Africa said on Thursday.
- SD Warren, Sappi's integrated U.S. paper producer, is embroiled in a labour dispute with the 250,000-strong United Paperworkers' International Union.
- The spectre of double digit inflation was spooked on Thursday by the lower-than-expected increase in last month's consumer price index, which rose 9.2 percent, economists said.
- The wheel is poised to turn full circle with the imminent announcement that Malbak is to sell its wholly-owned Tedelex subsidiary to Jack Cohen, its former executive chairman.
- Evidence unearthed by Witwatersrand police reporting officer, advocate Jan Munik, could result in the prosecution of up to 20 Brixton Murder and Robbery Unit detectives for assault and torture.
